item.research_question: How can machine learning and molecular dynamics be combined to predict the optimal composition, mechanical properties, and tension-compression asymmetry of FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloys, and what is the mechanism by which HEA coatings affect the mechanical properties of a nickel matrix?
item.material_system: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloys (specifically Fe33Ni32Cr11Co11Cu13) and Ni matrix with HEA coating
item.processing_route: Molecular dynamics simulations using LAMMPS with EAM potential; model size 3.56 × 7.12 × 3.56 nm³; relaxed at 300 K under NVT ensemble for 300 ps; strain rate 4 × 10⁻⁷ s⁻¹; time step 0.001 ps; Machine Learning using Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN), and Random Forest (RF) with 80% training/20% test split
item.test_conditions: Tensile and compressive loads applied in y direction at temperatures of 77 K, 300 K, 600 K, and 900 K; atomic content limits 5% to 35% for ML input
key_findings: The MLR model predicted an optimal composition of Fe33Ni32Cr11Co11Cu13 with a tensile strength of 28.25 GPa.
The error between the MLR predicted tensile strength (28.25 GPa) and the MD simulated tensile strength (28.38 GPa) was within 0.5%.
Tensile strength of FeNiCrCoCu HEA increased significantly with Ni content, while Co and Cu content showed a trend of increasing then decreasing strength.
Tension-compression asymmetry increased with temperature (40.5% at 77 K to 73.94% at 600 K) and Cu content, but decreased with Fe content.
Polycrystalline HEA tensile and compressive strengths decreased by 31.33% and 30.03% respectively at 300 K compared to single crystal HEA.
HEA coating increased Ni tensile strength from 2.3 GPa to 2.46 GPa and reduced Ni tension-compression asymmetry from 65.97% to 48.8%.
The MLR model achieved a prediction confidence of 84.9%, higher than BPNN (68.28%) and RF (74.94%).
item.mechanism: Tension-compression asymmetry is caused by twinning increasing stress during compression and dislocation slip reducing stress during tension; HEA coating reduces asymmetry in Ni by promoting dislocation climb and twin formation in the matrix, where different atomic sizes obstruct slip and stress concentration promotes twinning, while twin degradation at the interface reduces compressive strength.
item.limitations: The study relies on molecular dynamics simulations which may not capture all experimental complexities; the text notes that experimental methods require significant cost and time, implying the simulation is a substitute but does not explicitly state simulation limitations beyond the scope of the provided text.
quotes: The optimal multiple linear regression machine learning algorithm predicts that the optimal composition is Fe33Ni32Cr11Co11Cu13 high-entropy alloy, with a tensile strength of 28.25 GPa.
The error between the tensile strength predicted by machine learning and the tensile strength obtained by molecular dynamics simulation is within 0.5%.

Question: How can machine learning and molecular dynamics be combined to predict the optimal composition, mechanical properties, and tension-compression asymmetry of FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloys, and what is the mechanism by which HEA coatings affect the mechanical properties of a nickel matrix?. System: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloys (specifically Fe33Ni32Cr11Co11Cu13) and Ni matrix with HEA coating. Processing: Molecular dynamics simulations using LAMMPS with EAM potential; model size 3.56 × 7.12 × 3.56 nm³; relaxed at 300 K under NVT ensemble for 300 ps; strain rate 4 × 10⁻⁷ s⁻¹; time step 0.001 ps; Machine Learning using Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN), and Random Forest (RF) with 80% training/20% test split. Test conditions: Tensile and compressive loads applied in y direction at temperatures of 77 K, 300 K, 600 K, and 900 K; atomic content limits 5% to 35% for ML input. Findings: The MLR model predicted an optimal composition of Fe33Ni32Cr11Co11Cu13 with a tensile strength of 28.25 GPa.; The error between the MLR predicted tensile strength (28.25 GPa) and the MD simulated tensile strength (28.38 GPa) was within 0.5%.; Tensile strength of FeNiCrCoCu HEA increased significantly with Ni content, while Co and Cu content showed a trend of increasing then decreasing strength.; Tension-compression asymmetry increased with temperature (40.5% at 77 K to 73.94% at 600 K) and Cu content, but decreased with Fe content.; Polycrystalline HEA tensile and compressive strengths decreased by 31.33% and 30.03% respectively at 300 K compared to single crystal HEA.; HEA coating increased Ni tensile strength from 2.3 GPa to 2.46 GPa and reduced Ni tension-compression asymmetry from 65.97% to 48.8%.; The MLR model achieved a prediction confidence of 84.9%, higher than BPNN (68.28%) and RF (74.94%).. Mechanism: Tension-compression asymmetry is caused by twinning increasing stress during compression and dislocation slip reducing stress during tension; HEA coating reduces asymmetry in Ni by promoting dislocation climb and twin formation in the matrix, where different atomic sizes obstruct slip and stress concentration promotes twinning, while twin degradation at the interface reduces compressive strength.. Limitations: The study relies on molecular dynamics simulations which may not capture all experimental complexities; the text notes that experimental methods require significant cost and time, implying the simulation is a substitute but does not explicitly state simulation limitations beyond the scope of the provided text..
